items.title: Peptides are the latest wellness fad. What are they, and are they safe?
items.summary: An FDA advisory panel has recommended making six unapproved peptides more accessible through compounding pharmacies — but scientists warn that easier access does not mean these experimental products have been proven safe or effective.
items.zh: 肽是最新的健康时尚。它们是什么？它们安全吗？

items.title: When AI art has no author: Study finds generated images often can’t be traced to training data
items.summary: A new method for surgically removing training examples from a model reveals that as datasets grow, the link between what a model learns and what it produces dissolves.
items.zh: 当人工智能艺术没有作者时：研究发现生成的图像通常无法追溯到训练数据

items.title: Neanderthals may have trekked through the Saudi Arabian desert 55,000 years ago, farther south than experts thought possible
items.summary: Stone tools from a lakeside site in Saudi Arabia hint that Neanderthals were adapted to the arid Arabian interior, not just to cold places.
items.zh: 尼安德特人可能在 55,000 年前徒步穿越沙特阿拉伯沙漠，比专家认为的更南边

items.title: 'Beyond human intuition': AI designs chip components 500 times smaller than what engineers could ever imagine
items.summary: Three new AI-designed chip components are just a few micrometers long and go beyond what human engineers have previously envisaged.
items.zh: “超越人类直觉”：人工智能设计的芯片组件比工程师想象的小 500 倍

items.title: X-rays add new twist to narwhal's spiral tusk
items.summary: New study finds that the tusks have not one but two spirals, twisting in opposite directions.
items.zh: X射线为独角鲸的螺旋象牙增添了新的扭曲

items.title: The pace of climate change matters more than overall heat in the race to save key Atlantic currents, study finds
items.summary: The rate of global warming, rather than the extra heat itself, could determine whether a system of ocean currents known as the Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation will cross a tipping point, new research suggests.
items.zh: 研究发现，在拯救主要大西洋洋流的竞赛中，气候变化的速度比总体热量更重要

items.title: What Spider-Man gets right — and wrong — about turning off superpowers
items.summary: In 'Spider-Man: Brand New Day,' Peter Parker devises a superpower inhibitor based on a real therapy using RNA.
items.zh: 蜘蛛侠关于关闭超能力的正确和错误

items.title: Archaeologists discover Etruscan well that was ritually opened with offerings for a goddess — and 'closed' with human bodies
items.summary: An ancient Etruscan cult likely left burials and bronze artifacts in a well that was recently discovered in Italy.
items.zh: 考古学家发现了伊特鲁里亚井，在仪式上用供奉女神的祭品打开，并用人体“封闭”

items.title: As temperatures get hotter, pesticides are more dangerous to farmworkers
items.summary: Research shows heat amplifies the dangers of pesticides.
items.zh: 随着气温越来越高，农药对农场工人来说更加危险

items.title: Scientists may have finally proved that “empty” space isn’t really empty
items.summary: A magnetar’s colossal magnetic field may have revealed a quantum effect predicted by Werner Heisenberg nearly 90 years ago, in which seemingly empty space alters the behavior of light. If confirmed, the discovery could offer the first direct evidence of vacuum birefringence and open a new window int
items.zh: 科学家可能最终证明“空”的空间并不是真正空的

items.title: Einstein’s biggest “mistake” came back — and changed cosmology forever
items.summary: Einstein’s abandoned cosmological constant made a spectacular comeback when astronomers discovered that the universe’s expansion is accelerating. It now sits at the heart of our best cosmological model—a model that works extraordinarily well, yet may still be wrong.
items.zh: 爱因斯坦最大的“错误”又回来了——并永远改变了宇宙学

items.title: A therapy that “rewrites” childhood memories can ease fear of failure
items.summary: Childhood criticism can leave people carrying a fear of failure long into adulthood, but new research suggests those emotional patterns may be surprisingly flexible. Young adults who revisited painful memories through imagery-based therapy showed lasting reductions in fear, guilt, sadness, and stres
items.zh: “重写”童年记忆的疗法可以减轻对失败的恐惧

items.title: Theban tomb reveals how Egyptian burial trends evolved in time
items.summary: Practices shifted from individuals buried in coffins to reusing sites for later mummy interments.
items.zh: 底比斯古墓揭示了埃及埋葬趋势如何随时间演变

items.title: How 35 percent of US employees are left on the margins
items.summary: In a new book, Paul Osterman details his research finding more than one-third of the country’s workers are “disposable,” with little security or chance of job advancement.
items.zh: 35% 的美国员工为何处于边缘地位

items.title: The bacteria that make cheese taste so good may also benefit your gut
items.summary: Scientists studying three artisan British cheeses found that the microbes responsible for their distinctive flavors may also offer surprising benefits for gut health. As the cheeses matured, helpful bacteria transformed their aromas and textures while potentially producing compounds linked to reduce
items.zh: 让奶酪味道如此美味的细菌也可能有益于您的肠道

items.title: The Moon's shadow raced across the heart of Spain, and I was there to see it
items.summary: Here's what it was like watching a total solar eclipse 90 minutes north of Madrid.
items.zh: 月亮的影子掠过西班牙的心脏，我在那里看到了它

items.title: DNA shaper steers nervous system development
items.summary: A study of worms finds a protein that helps shape the structure of the genome is critical for establishing the identity of some neurons.
items.zh: DNA 塑造者引导神经系统发育

items.title: Mathematical framework connects biological principles to manufacturable, adaptive materials
items.summary: The new framework could streamline the design process of robotic grippers or aerospace components that exhibit complex behaviors found in nature.
items.zh: 数学框架将生物学原理与可制造的适应性材料联系起来

items.title: MIT engineers connect bacteria to create living transistors
items.summary: By wiring together colonies of these bacteria, the researchers built circuits that can perform complicated calculations.
items.zh: 麻省理工学院的工程师将细菌连接起来创造活的晶体管

items.title: Snail slime does many jobs thanks to calcium
items.summary: Snails have five distinct types of mucus, each with its own job. The mollusks tweak calcium secretions to get the chemical mixture just right.
items.zh: 蜗牛粘液富含钙，可以发挥多种作用

items.title: Theory of Fluids Enters the 21st Century
items.summary: From the 1800s to the early 2000s, physicists used the same theory to understand the behavior of fluids. Now, using a modern insight, they have redefined fluids from the bottom up. The post Theory of Fluids Enters the 21st Century first appeared on Quanta Magazine
items.zh: 流体理论进入 21 世纪

items.title: The COVID-19 vaccine may offer brain cancer patients a surprise benefit
items.summary: A recent shot of the COVID-19 vaccine doubled survival time in glioblastoma patients who had undergone tumor biopsy or surgery.
items.zh: COVID-19 疫苗可能会给脑癌患者带来意想不到的好处

items.title: Meet the only known trebuchet casualty in history
items.summary: "It highlights the brutality of medieval warfare," said paleopathologist Jo Buckberry.
items.zh: 认识历史上唯一已知的投石机伤亡者

items.title: Flexible brain circuits can switch between different tasks
items.summary: Neuroscientists have discovered circuits in the prefrontal cortex that can be repurposed to store different types of information.
items.zh: 灵活的大脑回路可以在不同的任务之间切换

items.title: Scientists turn DNA into a memory device that uses 100x less power
items.summary: Researchers combined synthetic DNA with a semiconductor to create an ultra-low-power memory device capable of storing and processing information in the same place. The bio-hybrid technology could eventually help make AI systems and next-generation computers far more energy efficient.
items.zh: 科学家将 DNA 转变为能耗降低 100 倍的存储设备

items.title: Scientists reveal why walking gets so much harder with age
items.summary: As we age, the body appears to sacrifice walking efficiency in exchange for stability. Older adults stiffen the ankle more with each step, which may help prevent falls but also forces the muscles to work harder while producing less forward motion. This leads to shorter strides, slower walking, and f
items.zh: 科学家揭示为什么随着年龄的增长行走变得越来越困难

items.title: How a brutal drought may have helped unleash yellow fever in Brazil
items.summary: Animals searching for water brought the forest to the city, perhaps sparking Brazil’s first yellow fever outbreak in decades.
items.zh: 严重干旱如何导致巴西黄热病爆发

items.title: A light-based scan could detect deadly bowel disease in preterm babies
items.summary: Necrotizing enterocolitis strikes premature babies with almost no warning. A new approach aims to detect it early with a quick, low-risk scan.
items.zh: 光扫描可以检测早产儿致命的肠道疾病

items.title: Why Aging May Be a Program, Not a Breakdown
items.summary: By deciphering the molecular signatures of millions of mouse cells, Junyue Cao has found that aging is not haphazard wear and tear but rather a “remodeling of the cell society.” The post Why Aging May Be a Program, Not a Breakdown first appeared on Quanta Magazine
items.zh: 为什么衰老可能是一个程序，而不是崩溃
